tagline: Delivering innovative medicines for people living with genetically defined conditions.
hero_kpi_rationale: Total revenue is the primary indicator of the company's overall financial performance, reflecting the success of its therapies and the expansion of its commercial portfolio.

kpis.name: Total revenues
kpis.explanation: Total amount of revenue generated by the company during a fiscal year.
kpis.description: Total revenue of $3.2 billion in 2025 shows significant growth compared to previous years, driven primarily by the expansion of VOXZOGO.

kpis.name: Cost of sales
kpis.explanation: Direct cost of goods or services sold by the company.
kpis.description: Cost of sales increased by 23.6% in 2025, outpacing revenue growth, which impacts gross margin.

kpis.name: Research and development investments
kpis.explanation: Expenses dedicated to the research and development of new products or technologies.
kpis.description: R&D investments increased notably by 23.4% in 2025, reflecting a strategy focused on future innovation.

kpis.name: Selling, general and administrative expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs related to selling, marketing, administration, and management of the company.
kpis.description: SG&A expenses increased by 14.3% in 2025, a growth that appears controlled relative to revenue growth.

kpis.name: Net income
kpis.explanation: Total profit of the company after deduction of all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income decreased by 18.2% in 2025, impacted by rising costs, restructuring charges, and expenses related to the acquisition of Amicus.

kpis.name: Amicus Acquisition Cost
kpis.explanation: Total cost of the acquisition of Amicus Therapeutics, Inc., a major transaction announced in December 2025.
kpis.description: The acquisition of Amicus for $4.8 billion represents a major strategic step to expand BioMarin's portfolio with two approved therapies for Fabry disease and Pompe disease.

kpis.name: Debt Financing for Amicus Acquisition
kpis.explanation: Amount of debt financing planned for the acquisition of Amicus, including bridge facility and senior notes.
kpis.description: Debt financing of $3.7 billion is planned for the Amicus acquisition through a senior secured bridge facility and other debt instruments, indicating significant leverage.
kpis.signal: High financial leverage to fund the acquisition.

kpis.name: Restructuring Charges
kpis.explanation: Costs related to restructuring, including the withdrawal of ROCTAVIAN from the market in December 2025.
kpis.description: Approximately $240 million in restructuring charges were recorded in 2025 following the strategic decision to withdraw ROCTAVIAN from the market, including asset impairments, inventory write-downs, and severance costs.
kpis.signal: Financial impact of a major strategic decision.

kpis.name: VOXZOGO Expansion
kpis.explanation: Significant expansion of VOXZOGO beyond achondroplasia into new indications.
kpis.description: The expansion of VOXZOGO was a significant contributor to total revenue of $3.2 billion in 2025, with year-over-year growth of 26.1%. Expansion includes new indications such as hypochondroplasia, Noonan syndrome, and SHOX deficiency.
kpis.signal: Key growth driver with revenues of $926.9 million in 2025.

kpis.name: Clinical Pipeline Advancement
kpis.explanation: Ongoing progression of drug candidates in BioMarin's clinical and preclinical pipeline.
kpis.description: The company continued to advance its pipeline of drug candidates in 2025, demonstrating ongoing commitment to innovation with R&D investments increasing by 23.4% to support the development of new therapies.
kpis.signal: Strategic focus on innovation and future growth.

kpis.name: Inozyme Acquisition
kpis.explanation: Acquisition of Inozyme Pharma in July 2025 to strengthen the portfolio of enzyme therapies.
kpis.description: The acquisition of Inozyme Pharma in July 2025 strengthened BioMarin's enzyme therapy portfolio by adding BMN 401 (formerly INZ-701), an advanced-stage enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of ENPP1 deficiency.
kpis.signal: Strategic strengthening of the enzyme therapy portfolio.

risks.title: Failure to execute corporate strategy
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned at the beginning of the 'Business and Operational Risks' section and repeated multiple times. The company emphasizes that failure could materially affect its financial condition and operations. The 'Industrial' category is weighted as it encompasses the overall strategy for development and commercialization.

risks.title: Failure in new product development
risks.score_rationale: Biopharmaceutical product development is described as 'highly costly and lengthy' with a 'high degree of risk' and outcomes 'inherently uncertain'. The inability to develop new products is an existential risk for a company in this sector, justifying maximum severity and the 'Industrial' category.

risks.title: Intensity of competition and failure against competitors
risks.score_rationale: This risk is strongly emphasized with repeated references to competition in development, commercialization, and obtaining regulatory approvals. The impact on revenue and the ability to justify development spending is significant. The 'Competition' category is central.

risks.title: Challenges related to acquisitions and integrations
risks.score_rationale: The company announced two major acquisitions in 2025 (Inozyme in July and Amicus in December for $4.8 billion). Risks related to integration, realization of synergies, and value dissipation are high. The growth strategy through acquisitions is central but carries significant operational and financial risks.

ai_positioning.summary: The company BMRN does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
